text:
alex: Heads-up — after the 6.4 kernel rollout in eu-west2 last night we're seeing a class of failures on P4 hosts: nvidia driver never probes and hosts hit oom_killer shortly after boot.

devon: Saw the same on a couple of canaries. dmesg shows DMA/IOMMU mapping errors.

jaya: Can you paste the dmesg lines? I want to see which symbol is failing.

alex: Paste below:
```
[    3.142857] nvidia: probe of 0000:00:1e.0 failed with error -12
[    3.142860] nvidia-nvlink: nvlink_core_register failed: -12
[    3.142865] vfio-pci 0000:00:1e.0: failed to setup DMA mapping: iommu_map failed
[    3.142870] Out of memory: Kill process 1234 (modprobe) score 500 or sacrifice child
```

infra-oncall: deploy-bot: kernel-rollout eu-west2 -> finished 2025-10-14T02:00Z :warning: (partial)

deploy-bot: kernel-rollout started on 120 hosts in eu-west2 (6.3 -> 6.4). Canary group size 10.

gabe: Looks like a DMA/IOMMU regression w/ vfio on 6.4 + our nvidia driver 525/535 combo. Might be the new IOMMU API changes.

maria: Impact: ~12% of GPU capacity in eu-west2 is currently offline (P4s). Provisioning queue backpressure is piling up and dedicated customers are seeing throttled allocation.

devon: Repro steps I ran locally on a repro host: boot 6.4, modprobe nvidia -> modprobe stalls, then modprobe killed by oom. Rebuilding DKMS drivers didn't change behavior.

jaya: Have we tried booting with iommu=pt or disabling iommu? That'll tell us if it's an IOMMU mapping change.

alex: I tried iommu=soft and iommu=pt on one canary. With iommu=pt the driver probes but NCCL tests show hangs during ncclCommInitRank (handshake timeouts).

gabe: Hm. Two separate failure modes: (1) outright DMA mapping failure and OOM; (2) driver probes but NCCL peer handshake timeouts. Could be kernel side change + subtle timing regression.

infra-oncall: Rolling task list:
- Rollback kernel on affected P4 pools to 5.15 (hotfix)
- Isolate canary subset and run extended kv-store + nccl smoke for 2h
- Collect full kdump/dmesg and bpf traces on failing hosts
- Coordinate with Nvidia on driver+kernel combo

maria: Ops ask: What is hit on customer SLAs and cost? If we keep rollback, we'll delay other host security updates but restore capacity. If we keep 6.4 and mitigate, we might lose more hosts and pay for burst capacity (spot/extra warm-up).

devon: Quick numbers — rollback will restore ~95% of P4 capacity in ~45m (reboot + verify). Keeping 6.4 keeps us ~12% short and increases provisioning latency by ~2x for GPU jobs -> estimated $7k/day in additional burst/priority allocation for the next week.

jaya: For immediate mitigation we should: pin affected pools to kernel 5.15, set scheduler to avoid P4 placements for time being, and open priority ticket with Nvidia.

alex: I've kicked off rollback playbook on the P4 pool (eu-west2). Starting with the least-loaded racks to avoid churn.

deploy-bot: rollback-job 4723 started (targets: p4-pool-eu-west2-partial)

gabe: Also let's collect: /proc/interrupts, lspci -vvv, and nv-hostengine logs. If anyone adds a repro diff test, include qemu/iommu varients.

maria: Noted. I'll update the incident doc and ping growth for customer comms (we need to warn a couple of Dedicated customers).

devon: Follow-up: I pushed a small kernel boot param experiment to one rack: add "pcie_aspm=off iommu.passthrough=0" — driver still fails to probe in most hosts but one rack moved to the NCCL-hang mode (driver up but comms flaky).

jaya: That suggests two knobs: iommu behavior and PCI link power state. Interesting. Could be a timing fallback in our firmware for P4s.

infra-oncall: Action items assigned: alex (orchestrate rollback), devon (collect traces + mini-repro), jaya (run pci/iommu boot matrix on canaries), gabe (open Nvidia support ticket + attach traces), maria (customer comms + cost impact calc).

alex: I'll also schedule a canary run on us-central1 to confirm whether this is region-specific or fleet-wide. So far only eu-west2 with the 6.4 rollout shows failures.

gabe: Putting this as high priority with Nvidia. If driver-team can't repro with kernel symbols, we'll need to test a few 6.x minors (6.2/6.3/6.5 rc) to find the offending change.

maria: FYI finance requests a rough estimate of additional spend if we keep rollback vs. patch route; I'll share numbers in 30m.

infra-oncall: Update: rollback is ~40% complete. 60 hosts left. No new host flapping so far.

devon: Found one clue in kconfig diff: a change in iommu_dma mapping path between 6.3 and 6.4 that affects vfio iommu_map path. Working on a minimal repro patch to show to Nvidia/kernel folks.

alex: Thanks — please dump traces to the shared S3 under s3://redwood-debug/eu-west2/kernel6x-p4s/1768504321/ and post links here.

maria: I'll post customer-facing note once rollback completes and we have a postmortem plan.

infra-oncall: Will follow up in #incidents once we have Nvidia response. For now, keep oncall rotation informed.

alex: tl;dr: kernel 6.4 rollout caused multiple GPU module failure modes on P4 fleet in eu-west2. Rolling back to 5.15 for affected hosts to restore capacity while we triage kernel+driver interaction.

maria: :thumbsup: keep updates coming.
